description.text: Domino’s is the largest pizza company in the world with more than 22,100 locations in over 90 markets around the world as of December 28, 2025, and operates two distinct service models within its stores, with a significant business in both delivery and carryout. We are a highly recognized global brand, and we focus on value while serving neighborhoods locally through our large worldwide network of franchise owners and U.S. Company-owned stores through both the delivery and carryout service models. We have been selling quality, affordable food to our customers since 1960. We became “Domino’s Pizza” in 1965 and opened our first franchised store in 1967. Over the past 65 years, we have built Domino’s into one of the most widely-recognized consumer brands in the world. We believe our commitment to value, convenience, quality and new products continues to keep consumers engaged with the brand. We are primarily a franchisor, with approximately 99% of Domino’s global stores owned and operated by our independent franchisees as of December 28, 2025. Franchising enables an individual to be a business owner and maintain control over all employment-related matters and pricing decisions, while also benefiting from the strength of the Domino’s global brand and operating system with limited capital investment by us.

about.description_short: Founded in 1960, Domino's Pizza is the largest pizza company in the world, with a significant business in both delivery and carryout. It ranks among the world's top public restaurant brands with a global enterprise of more than 22,700 stores in over 90 markets. Domino's had global retail sales of over $20.7 billion in the trailing four quarters ended September 6, 2026. Its system is comprised of independent franchise owners who accounted for 99% of Domino's stores as of the end of the third quarter of 2026. In the U.S., Domino's generated more than 85% of U.S. retail sales in 2025 via digital channels and has developed many innovative ordering platforms.

analysis_md:
# DPZ — Domino’s Pizza, Inc.
Pass-1 v5 run, 2026-10-19 (engine release 5.4.0). All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The world's largest pizza company: 22,706 stores in ~90 markets at the end of Q3 2026, ~99% franchised. The franchisor earns franchise royalties and fees, supply-chain sales to its own stores (food, equipment), and advertising-fund contributions, plus a small company-owned store segment. Asset-light by design — the franchisees own the stores and most of the capital.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $4,939,994,000; operating income $953,974,000; net income $601,704,000; operating cash flow $792,062,000; capex $120,558,000; SBC $44,640,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $626,864,000 = $18.31/share** (latest FY OE/share, key_numbers.md).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): **not usable for this company.** It prints +$1,633,323,000 for FY2024 and −$518,511,000 for FY2025 because its ΔNWC leg (−$1,049,153,000 in FY2024, +$1,120,215,000 in FY2025) is dominated by a securitized-debt reclassification — debt_current was $1,149,679,000 at FY2024-end and $6,131,000 at FY2025-end as a tranche moved back to long-term. That is a financing reclass, not working capital. The OCF-based conservative series is the clean one and is used throughout.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Net debt $4,691,139,000 (key_numbers.md). Buybacks continue: share count CAGR −1.75%/yr, already credited in the growth blend via the +1.75pp share adjustment, not double-counted.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q3 2026 (period ended 2026-09-06), from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $792,062,000 − prior YTD $552,256,000 + current YTD $520,601,000 = **TTM $760,407,000**
- Capex: FY $120,558,000 − prior YTD $56,667,000 + current YTD $60,829,000 = **TTM $124,720,000**
- SBC: FY $44,640,000 − prior YTD $31,681,000 + current YTD $30,843,000 = **TTM $43,802,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **33,416,210**
- **TTM OE total $591,885,000 → base OE/share $17.71** (base_source: ttm_json). Cross-check: fundamentals.json's independent TTM build prints OE/share $17.66 on the same period.
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is $13.40/share — rejected as the base for the reason under BASE_DIVERGENCE below; it is still reported in key_numbers.md.

## Moat: 7/10 — strong franchisor moat, capped by a mature category
Justification: global brand, proprietary ordering/technology platform, supply-chain scale and long-term franchise agreements give a strong, durable franchisor moat with high cash returns on minimal franchisor capital; capped at 7 because consumers face near-zero switching costs in a mature category, pricing power is value-limited, growth now comes mainly from new stores rather than same-store sales, and master-franchisee stress drags international results.
- FOR: Global brand and scale — largest pizza QSR, 22,706 stores in ~90 markets; asset-light franchisor model (~99% franchised, royalties plus supply-chain sales, capex only ~2.4% of revenue); proprietary technology/ordering platform and loyalty program driving order frequency; supply-chain scale and procurement productivity (supply-chain gross margin 12.2% in Q3 2026, +0.9pp YoY, from the Q3 2026 report); long-term franchise agreements and fortressing density raise franchisee switching friction; durable margins through cycles — operating margin 16.9% → 19.3% and gross margin 36.3% → 40.0% over the last five fiscal years in fundamentals.json, OE positive 5/5 years.
- AGAINST: Consumers have near-zero switching costs; pizza is a mature, promotion-driven category; value positioning limits pricing power (U.S. pricing +1.2% in Q3 2026; average ticket fell in Q2 2026 on a failed premium launch); same-store sales have stalled (U.S. +0.3%, international +0.2% in Q3 2026, with a guidance cut at that print); master-franchisee stress at Domino's Pizza Enterprises drags international SSS and store growth; aggregator platforms are both a channel and a competing gatekeeper; high financial leverage (net debt $4,691,139,000; company-reported leverage ratio 4.2x EBITDA at Q3 2026).
- ROIC note (required evidence): the `roic_proxy` series in fundamentals.json prints 0.79–0.99 over the last five fiscal years, but it is **not** taken at face value — book equity is deeply negative (−$3,901,142,000 at FY2025-end in financials_history.csv) after decades of buybacks, so the equity + debt − cash denominator is artificially tiny and the ratio is mechanically inflated. The moat score rests on the franchise economics above (royalty stream on franchisee capital, stable-to-rising margins), not on that ratio.
- A 7 gives CAP = 11.1 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 11.1 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
Growth sanity check (mandatory): the engine blend is 6.09% (rev CAGR 5y 3.72%, rev CAGR 3y 2.89%, latest rev YoY 4.96%, OE/share CAGR 2y 20.37% — the last is an artifact of the FY2025 OCF step-up and does not drive the median-based blend). Against actual prints: FY2025 revenue +4.96%, Q2 2026 revenue +4.3%, Q3 2026 revenue +3.4% with operating income +8.3% and EPS +12.7% (buyback-assisted); 2026 guidance was cut at the Q3 print to mid-single-digit operating-income growth with U.S. SSS at the low end of low-single digits and international SSS ~flat, against a long-term algorithm of ~8% operating-income growth. The default scenario offsets (−12/+12pp) would have started super-bull at 18.1% — above every recent print including buyback-assisted EPS growth — so the offsets were compressed to −0.10/−0.04/0/+0.04/+0.08, giving starts of −3.9% / 2.1% / **6.1%** / 10.1% / 14.1%. The base start (6.1%) sits between the revenue prints (~3–5%) and guided operating-income growth, which is where OE/share has actually been landing; the super-bull start (14.1%) is set just above Q3's +12.7% EPS print as a genuine stretch case, with a written reason rather than the unanchored 18.1% default. Probabilities were shifted one notch bearish vs default (15/25/30/20/10) for the Q3 guidance cut, flat SSS, and the leverage under HIGH_NET_DEBT. OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $305.05.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | -3.9% | 0.75 | SSS turn negative, franchisee economics break, leverage bites | $80.68 | 5.49% |
| Bear | 25% | 2.1% | 0.90 | Store growth only; SSS ~flat as in Q3 2026, guidance-cut trajectory sticks | $128.24 | 7.73% |
| Base | 30% | 6.1% | 1.00 | Mid-single-digit operating growth plus buybacks, normal fade over the CAP | $172.13 | 9.73% |
| Bull | 20% | 10.1% | 1.10 | Long-term ~8% operating-income algorithm restored, plus share shrink | $228.91 | 12.13% |
| Super bull | 10% | 14.1% | 1.25 | SSS reaccelerate, aggregator/loyalty compounding, margin expansion continues | $314.61 | 15.34% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $173.04 (−43.3% vs price), IV@12% $231.55, IV@10% $297.09, weighted IRR 9.81%, base-case IRR 9.73%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 5.81%, terminal value 19.5% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.90x, net debt 7.74x normalized OE, 9.7 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through the Q3 2026 period ended 2026-09-06, legs quoted above.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY OE/share $18.31 vs 3-yr median $13.40): both are partly distorted, in opposite directions, and the median is the bigger problem. The latest FY is mildly flattered: FY2025 OCF rose to $792,062,000 from $624,897,000 while net income only rose to $601,704,000 from $584,170,000 — part of the step-up is working-capital / advertising-fund timing (the same timing ran in reverse in Q3 2026, when YTD free cash flow fell 7.2% on advertising-payment timing per the Q3 report). But the step-up mostly persists: TTM OCF is $760,407,000 and TTM OE/share $17.71, with fundamentals.json's TTM OE/share growth at +0.64% YoY — flat against FY2025, not collapsing back to the median. The median ($13.40) is dragged by the FY2023–24 bases ($12.65 and $13.40/share) from the soft-OCF years. Verdict: use the TTM base ($17.71), which sits below the flattered latest FY and well above the stale median.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 7.74x normalized OE): real and structural — this is a leveraged franchisor by design (whole-business securitized debt; total debt $4,816,814,000 against cash $125,675,000 at FY2025-end, net debt $4,691,139,000; company-reported leverage 4.2x EBITDA at Q3 2026). The debt is largely fixed-rate and serviced by a royalty stream that has stayed OE-positive through every year in the history, but the equity is a thin stub: a sustained SSS decline hits OE/share with operating and financial leverage at once. Handled by the bearish-shifted probabilities, the 0.75 super-bear OE multiplier, and sizing the verdict to the bear end.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier D at 7.73% vs bull tier C at 12.13%): the verdict is sized to the bear end — even the bull case only reaches Tier C, and no scenario except super-bull (10% weight) clears 15%. The tier is D on the weighted numbers and stays D on any single-scenario reading except the super-bull tail.

## My thoughts / overlay
- This is a quality/price split, not a quality debate: the franchise machine (asset-light royalties, 5/5 OE-positive years, margins expanding, DPS and buybacks funded from OE) is exactly the kind of business the sweep wants to own — at a price that pays for it. At $305.05 the market is capitalizing the bull-to-super-bull path; the weighted IV@15% is $173.04.
- Method range: on the stale 3-yr median base ($13.40) with default offsets, the preliminary run printed weighted IRR 8.30% and IV@15% $136.53 — also Tier D. On the TTM base the answer moves to 9.81% / $173.04, still Tier D. The tier is robust to the base dispute; only the hurdle price moves (~$137–$173 for 15%).
- Watch items: whether SSS reaccelerate after the Q3 2026 guidance cut (U.S. +0.3%, international +0.2%); franchisee profitability (the U.S. net-store target was cut to 125–150 for 2026 on pipeline/franchisee pressure); Domino's Pizza Enterprises' drag on international; the CEO transition (Joe Jordan took over October 1, 2026); and debt maturities against the 4.2x leverage ratio.
- Margin of safety: there is none at this price on these numbers — the price sits 43.3% above the weighted IV@15% and above even the bull-case IV@15% ($228.91). Only the 10%-weighted super-bull IV@15% ($314.61) exceeds the price.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 9.81% on the TTM base; bear→bull band D→C, sized to the bear end)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the TTM base and flag resolutions; the scenario spread is 3.90x and the growth path after the Q3 guidance cut is genuinely uncertain)
- One-liner: High-quality franchisor, moat 7/10, but at $305.05 it does not clear 15%: weighted IRR 9.81% on the TTM base, weighted IV@15% $173.04 — it only clears the 15% hurdle below ~$173, so Tier D despite the franchise quality.
